name: LCRS B101120.1-024053 (Hubble)
blurb: LCRS B101120.1-024053, a post-starburst (E+A) galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: gal101352025547-hubble
story: Post-starburst galaxies like this one are among the best candidates for galaxies in transition, turning from gas-rich and star-forming to gas-poor and passively evolving through galaxy mergers. This one is among the most disk-like of its kind, and earlier ground-based images show a smooth disk crossed by a dust lane.

claims.text: The target position (10 13 52, -02 55 47) is the E+A galaxy LCRS B101120.1-024053 (EA17)
Post-starburst (E+A) galaxies are the best candidates for galaxies in transition from gas-rich and star-forming to gas-poor and passively evolving, via galaxy mergers
The E+A galaxies EA06 to EA21 of the Zabludoff et al. (1996) Las Campanas Redshift Survey sample were imaged with Hubble's ACS
EA17 is one of the most disky E+A galaxies in the sample
EA17 has a smooth appearance but contains a dust lane
